method: Evidence from the release files, compared with the reviewed 1.11.0; one Sonnet 5.5 agent established the facts with exact quotes; every quote checked against the release files and README by script; the facts that set the level checked again by hand; level from the fixed rule; label and summary written by Claude Opus 5.5.
label: Downloads and runs the OpenDataLoader PDF parser the first time you translate a PDF
summary: The first time you translate a PDF's full text, it downloads the OpenDataLoader PDF parser (a 24 MB Java program), usually from a PyPI mirror in China, and runs it, showing a progress window but not asking; the README now says it is downloaded on first use. We checked that its fingerprint matches the parser in the project's own release. If you don't have Java, it asks first, then downloads a Java runtime from Adoptium's site or a Chinese mirror of it, checked against Adoptium's checksum.

facts.what: Two downloads for the 'Translate full text' / 'Translate and open side by side' PDF pipeline. (1) The OpenDataLoader PDF parser, opendataloader-pdf-cli 2.5.17 (a Java jar, 24,243,150 bytes; the wheel/zip carrying it is about 22.7 MB), fetched on first PDF parse because this xpi does not bundle it; the plugin extracts the jar into its data folder and runs it with `java -jar`. (2) A Java 17 runtime (Eclipse Temurin JRE, about 40-50 MB) from Adoptium or a mirror of it, only if no Java 11+ is found, unpacked into the Zotero profile and used to run that jar.
urls: https://mirrors.nju.edu.cn/adoptium and https://mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/Adoptium (JRE mirrors, used only with Adoptium's checksum)
facts.publisher: the OpenDataLoader project, which makes opendataloader-pdf
facts.readmeQuote: on first use they are downloaded automatically
facts.notes: OpenDataLoader is the maker of the PDF parser jar (github.com/opendataloader-project/opendataloader-pdf), NOT the plugin's developer (repo is Liozhang/z-transplit). The scanner's 'official' source is the GitHub-release fallback only (url at ztransplit.js 13848). Default order (OdlJarDownloader, 13833-13990 and runDownload 13994): probe every source with a Range request, rank by latency (13856), try fastest first; sources are now six PyPI mirrors for the wheel (aliyun, tuna, tencent, huawei, ustc, and files.pythonhosted.org, 14081-14088; only when WHEEL_PACKAGE_HASH_PATH has the version, 14077-14080 has 2.5.0 and 2.5.17), then the GitHub release zip. So the usual first source is a Chinese PyPI mirror (third-party by the brief's definition), which is why source is third-party. Integrity differs per download. JAR: PINNED. core/pdf/lib/PROVENANCE.json inside the xpi holds sha256 ac1feeaac083eb70fe44d7051d1938d7cce7f639d2381604f5b971c0e7abfad6 and bytes 24243150 (version 2.5.17); runDownload throws 'no pinned SHA-256 in provenance' if absent (13997), and installJarFromArchive (13916) extracts the jar entry and does `if (hash !== meta.sha256) { throw ...jar checksum mismatch` (13961-13963) before moving it into place; the hash is of the extracted jar, not of the zip/wheel. JRE: SAME-SOURCE CHECKSUM: queryAdoptiumLatestAsset (13384-13405) reads pkg.link and pkg.checksum from the api.adoptium.net assets JSON; buildJreSources (13409) now lists the Nanjing University and Tsinghua Adoptium mirrors (JRE_MIRRORS, 13815-13816) as well as Adoptium itself, and downloadJRE (13557) compares the sha256 of the archive to Adoptium's checksum for every source (13660-13662), trying the next source on a mismatch. If the assets API fails, only Adoptium's own binary/latest URL is used with NO checksum (asset.sha256 undefined; archive just written, 13700 skips the record). I keep same-source-checksum (the weaker), and the JRE has a no-check fallback. TRIGGER: also two paths, unchanged. Jar: PDF parse calls getJarPath (14636), which, when the jar is absent from the xpi (this lean xpi ships only core/pdf/lib/ztransplit-region-text-remover.jar plus the two PROVENANCE files; PROVENANCE says the lean xpi does not carry the jar and OdlJarDownloader downloads it on first parse) calls downloadPinnedJar (14713) with a progress window titled 'Downloading the OpenDataLoader parsing component' (makeJarDownloadProgress, 14507); no confirmation dialog, so automatic-on-feature-use (right-click PDF > 'Translate full text (save as attachment)' or reader 'Translate and open side by side'). Java: handleMissingJava (71794) only runs when Java is missing (call sites 71965 and 72297) and shows a Services.prompt.confirmEx dialog 'Java required' whose body says it 'fetches the ~40 MB Java runtime and extracts it' with buttons 'Download and install' / 'Open download page' / 'Cancel' -> asks-first for that part. Most concerning kept: automatic-on-feature-use. RUN: Java is launched with `java -jar <odl jar>` (15358). README (v1.21.1, lines 34-38) now says: 'The slim installer (the default download) does not bundle the ~24 MB layout-parsing component or the ~43 MB Java runtime: on first use they are downloaded automatically by racing several mirrors concurrently, and the bytes must pass the official SHA-256 checksum before anything is installed', so toldInReadme is now yes (was partly in 1.11.0, whose README had no such note). Changed from 1.11.0: the parser is 2.5.17 (was 2.5.0) with a new pinned hash; three more PyPI mirrors (Tencent, Huawei, USTC); two JRE mirrors (NJU, Tuna) added beside Adoptium; README tells about the download. Unchanged: both triggers, the pinned-jar check, Adoptium checksum, the confirm dialog, the run command. A scan of every https URL in the scripts found no other new download (the new URLs are translation-API endpoints and the mirrors above). The -full.xpi build is a separate asset.
facts.reviewerNote: Level set by the parser jar: its SHA-256 (ac1feeaa...) is in the xpi's core/pdf/lib/PROVENANCE.json and installJarFromArchive refuses a mismatch, whichever mirror served it; checked by hand 2026-11-16 that the jar inside opendataloader-pdf-cli-2.5.17.zip from the project's GitHub release (zip SHA-256 09ba7810..., matching GitHub's own digest) and the jar inside the PyPI wheel opendataloader_pdf-2.5.17-py3-none-any.whl (wheel SHA-256 d3dd0869..., matching PyPI's digest, path 89/95/5fa96e... equal to WHEEL_PACKAGE_HASH_PATH) both have that SHA-256 and 24,243,150 bytes. The Java runtime comes from Adoptium (its maker) or a Chinese mirror of it, after a confirmEx dialog, checked against a checksum from Adoptium's API when that API answers. This review is of the lean z-transplit.xpi; the -full.xpi build carries the jar and downloads nothing.
